*** Add File: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/agent-docs/jusprin/left-pane-implementation-handoff.md
+# JusPrin Plates / Project pane implementation handoff
+
+Implement the approved native **Plates / Project** pane in JusPrin's Prepare workspace. The Figma frames listed below are the visual source of truth; this document supplies the behavior, data ownership, integration constraints, and verification that static mockups cannot express.
+
+The pane stays visible for simple and complex projects. The collapsed-pane exploration in frame **26g** is deliberately out of scope and must not be implemented.
+
+## Design source
+
+- Figma file: [JusPrin v2](https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2)
+- Page: **Plates & Project Pane**
+- Implement the named frames below. Use their layers, variables, existing component instances, dimensions, spacing, states, and copy directly from Figma instead of recreating the visuals from prose.
+
+| Figma frame | Implementation state |
+| --- | --- |
+| `26a · Ordinary two-plate job · Plates` | Default two-plate state |
+| `26b · Complex plate · Plates` | Copies, materials, modifier/negative part, disabled copy, mesh errors, and Not on a plate |
+| `26c1 · One plate, one object` | Minimum-content state; the pane still remains visible |
+| `26c2 · Folded plate summaries` | Computed summaries for inactive folded plates |
+| `26d1 · Plate row menu` | Plate overflow menu |
+| `26d2 · Object row menu` | Object overflow menu |
+| `26e1 · Project with metadata` | Project root with 3MF metadata |
+| `26e2 · Project details` | Full metadata and attachment entry points |
+| `26e3 · Project print history` | Detailed physical-print records plus a count-only older record |
+| `26e4 · Count-only print history` | Projects whose older prints have only a count |
+| `26f · Project without metadata` | Honest no-metadata state |
+| `26h · Customization mark comparison` | Decision record; implement the recommended `h2` single-mark treatment |
+
+Do not implement `26g`, a collapse rail, a collapse control, or any persistence for a collapsed state. Do not restore the old 25-series pane mockups.
+
+## Product boundary
+
+Build this as a fork-owned native wxWidgets surface under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. OrcaSlicer's project model, plate list, selection, slicing results, undo history, context actions, project metadata, and serialization remain authoritative.
+
+The pane presents and invokes those owners. It must not create a second project model, infer project facts from labels or canvas coordinates, simulate clicks against hidden controls, or add a separate undo path.
+
+Keep these controls in their current homes:
+
+- model import;
+- printer, nozzle, and material setup;
+- Slice and Print;
+- move, rotate, scale, and other spatial tools;
+- the Agent conversation.
+
+Do not add permanent action rows for operations that belong in the plate or object overflow menu.
+
+## Plates tab behavior
+
+### Plate and selection state
+
+- Show every plate, including a one-plate project.
+- Keep the active plate expanded. Keep all other plates folded.
+- Selecting a plate row activates the same Orca plate in the 3D view.
+- Selecting an object, copy, part, modifier, negative part, or support volume selects that exact Orca item when Orca supports that selection granularity.
+- Reflect selection changes made in the 3D view back into the pane without delay or stale highlights.
+- Switching between Plates and Project must not change the active plate or canvas selection.
+- Clear project-scoped IDs and pane expansion state when `project_session` changes.
+
+### Plate rows and folded summaries
+
+- Derive **Sliced** versus **Needs slice** from the current authoritative slice state.
+- A folded plate summary is computed from current plate membership. It is not editable text and is not stored separately.
+- If a plate contains one distinct object, show its name and total copy count when greater than one.
+- If a plate contains several distinct objects, show the object count used by Figma.
+- Include disabled copies in the total. Append the separate **N won't print** phrase when applicable.
+- Show lock or customized-plate-settings indicators only when those facts apply.
+- **Add plate** must call Orca's existing plate creation path and participate in Orca undo/redo.
+
+### Object rows and hierarchy
+
+- Show the object name and copy count.
+- Show filament/color assignment only for a multi-material job or an object-specific override.
+- Make a disabled object's or copy's **won't print** state explicit.
+- Show **Not on a plate** only when at least one object instance belongs to no plate. Membership comes from `PartPlateList`, not bounding-box guesses made by the pane.
+- A simple object remains one row.
+- Add disclosure children only for data that exists: copies, model parts, modifiers, negative parts, support enforcers, or support blockers.
+- Do not introduce a permanent synthetic assembly level.
+- Keep intentional customization separate from mesh problems. Implement the recommended `h2` treatment in frame 26h: one gray customization mark opens the list of applicable Orca tools/settings. Mesh problems use the distinct error treatment in Figma.
+
+### Context menus
+
+Use the menu contents and ordering from frames 26d1 and 26d2. Route every command to Orca's existing behavior rather than reimplementing it in the pane.
+
+Plate menu:
+
+- Rename
+- Arrange
+- Auto-orient
+- Lock or Unlock
+- Plate settings
+- Delete plate
+- Show Move to front and filament grouping only when their existing Orca preconditions apply.
+
+Object menu:
+
+- Use Orca's existing object context actions for quantity, printability, filament, per-object settings, repair, split, rename, and delete.
+- A copy row exposes the same relevant menu path for that copy.
+- Right-clicking a row and clicking its overflow button must open the same menu model.
+
+## Project tab behavior
+
+### Identity and metadata
+
+- The saved JusPrin project name and save state come from managed project persistence. They are not the model title stored in the 3MF.
+- The model title, designer/author, license, description, profile metadata, cover images, and packed files come from Orca's project metadata and `Workspace::ProjectDetails`.
+- Never synthesize a model title from the project name or source filename.
+- Omit missing metadata. Do not render blank fields or placeholders.
+- When no model metadata exists, use frame 26f exactly and keep **Edit Project Info** available.
+- **Details** opens the nested pane view in frame 26e2. Show only sections backed by data.
+- Attachment categories should map to Orca's existing packed-file categories. Bill of materials, assembly guide, images, and other files remain Orca project attachments; do not copy them into a second store.
+- **Edit Project Info** opens Orca's existing project-information editor.
+
+### Project root actions
+
+- **Printed N times** opens print history.
+- **Details** opens project details.
+- **Version history** opens the existing managed autosave history and preserves its current restore confirmation, pinning, validation, and failure behavior.
+- **Export project 3MF…** opens the existing system save dialog and uses `ProjectAutosave::export_copy`. It is separate from exporting G-code or a sliced 3MF.
+- Moving these entry points from `StatusRow` must preserve current functionality and error handling. Recent projects and Preferences may remain in the header overflow menu.
+
+### Nested navigation
+
+- A Project subview uses the back action shown in Figma to return to the Project root.
+- Escape goes up one Project level when a subview is open.
+- Escape at the Project root does not switch to Plates.
+- Clicking the Plates tab always returns directly to the plate list while preserving plate and object selection.
+- A new project starts on the Project root. Do not show a subview retained from the previous project.
+
+## Print history truthfulness
+
+`Agent::ProjectStateDocument::physical_prints()` is the authoritative physical-print ledger. Do not construct history from slice events, exports, or UI activity.
+
+- The root count comes from `physical_print_count()`.
+- A detailed row may show only fields present in its `PhysicalPrintRecord`: timestamps, plate, printer, outcome, and related recorded facts.
+- Duration may be derived only when both recorded timestamps are valid.
+- Material weight, cost, and predicted time in `SliceStatistics` are slice/build estimates. Label them as estimates as shown in frame 26e3; never present them as measured physical consumption or duration.
+- Do not add a currency symbol unless the persisted record identifies the currency. A bare stored cost is not enough to guess dollars.
+- Omit any missing field instead of substituting zero or placeholder copy.
+- Preserve count-only history for migrated/older data. Use frame 26e4 when no detailed records exist, and the count-only row from 26e3 when detailed and legacy records coexist.
+- Map outcomes to localized user-facing labels without losing the persisted distinction among `completed`, `failed`, and `cancelled`.
+- Subscribe to ledger changes without taking away the listener needed by another shell component. If the existing single-listener persistence API cannot support both `StatusRow` and the pane during migration, replace it with safe multi-subscriber ownership before moving the count.
+
+## Current code map and known gaps
+
+Start with the canonical documents in `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`. Before changing an OrcaSlicer-owned file, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`.
+
+Likely integration points:
+
+- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp` and `.hpp`: place the fork-owned pane as the left sibling of the existing workspace. Keep the stock Notebook pages and Agent-pane lifecycle intact.
+- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/Workspace.hpp`: extend the fork-owned projection with the smallest behavior-oriented data and commands the pane needs.
+- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp`: read current plate membership, slice state, selection, object hierarchy, metadata, and customization facts; delegate mutations to their Orca owners.
+- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectState.hpp`: refresh on Selection, Objects, Plates, Project, Settings, History, Transform, undo/redo, slicing, and project replacement as relevant.
+- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp`: migrate Project entry points and print count after the pane owns them, without changing Recent projects, Preferences, or unrelated header behavior.
+- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ManufacturingHistory.hpp` and `ProjectStateDocument.hpp`: read physical-print records and counts.
+- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/CanvasPresentationController.cpp`: keep the legacy Orca sidebar and plate overlays hidden; the new pane supplies visible navigation.
+- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Canvas/ViewportToolStrip.cpp`: preserve the existing object tools and right-click path.
+
+The current workspace snapshot is not sufficient for every approved row. Confirm and close these gaps before building presentation code around assumptions:
+
+1. `WorkspacePlate::objects` does not expose per-instance IDs, per-instance printability, or off-plate instances.
+2. `ObjectDetails` exposes counts but not the named child rows needed for parts, modifiers, negative parts, or support volumes.
+3. Plate selection and all row-menu commands do not yet share one public UI command surface.
+4. Intentional customization needs explicit facts for support painting, color painting, variable layer height, per-object overrides, and plate settings.
+5. Mesh repair/problem status needs a stable read model separate from customization state.
+6. Project metadata exposes attachment identifiers and categories; the pane still needs the existing Orca paths that open each detail or attachment.
+
+Expose the smallest strict API that represents each missing fact or command. Keep preconditions in the caller that owns the workflow and let unexpected failures remain visible.
+
+## Design-system and component rules
+
+Follow `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` before writing UI code.
+
+- Every color, radius, font, and control size comes from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json` through `ShellTheme` or `ShellRecipes`.
+- Layout gaps use the documented spacing scale.
+- If a required value has no token, add the token and its guard before using it.
+- Reuse established generic primitives such as icons, icon buttons, tabs, menus, swatches, typography, and selection treatments.
+- Keep feature-specific plate rows, object rows, metadata blocks, and history records as pane-owned composition unless another production surface already has the same reusable contract.
+- Do not add Figma-style specimen components or one-off variants to the production design system merely because several mockup frames repeat a structure.
+- Support light and dark themes, keyboard focus, localization, and 100%, 150%, and 200% display scaling.
+
+## Suggested implementation order
+
+1. Add tests for the missing read model: plate membership, per-copy printability, folded summaries, off-plate instances, hierarchy counts/children, customization facts, and mesh-problem status.
+2. Add the smallest workspace commands for plate selection/addition and menu actions that do not already have a fork-owned seam.
+3. Build the pane shell and tab/navigation state using frame 26c1 first.
+4. Add the ordinary and folded multi-plate states from 26a and 26c2.
+5. Add complex object hierarchy and conditional indicators from 26b and 26h.
+6. Route the menus from 26d1 and 26d2 to existing Orca actions.
+7. Add the Project root and metadata states from 26e1, 26e2, and 26f.
+8. Move version history/export/details/count entry points from `StatusRow` only after their pane replacements pass end-to-end tests.
+9. Add print history from the persisted ledger using 26e3 and 26e4.
+10. Run visual and behavioral verification across supported platforms and scaling levels.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+### Behavior
+
+- One plate and one object still show the pane and both tabs.
+- Plate selection, object selection, canvas selection, active plate, and row highlights stay synchronized in both directions.
+- Folded summaries remain correct after add, delete, duplicate, disable, move between plates, arrange, undo/redo, project restore, and project replacement.
+- Simple objects stay simple. Child rows appear only for existing copies, parts, modifiers, negative parts, and support volumes.
+- Not on a plate appears only with real off-plate content.
+- Every plate and object menu action reaches the existing Orca behavior and undo history.
+- Project name and 3MF model title never substitute for one another.
+- Missing metadata uses 26f without invented or blank values.
+- Version restore and project export preserve existing confirmations, validation, and failure behavior.
+- Print history displays only persisted facts and clearly labeled estimates.
+- Frame 26g behavior is absent.
+
+### Visual and accessibility
+
+- Compare every implemented state against its named Figma frame.
+- Verify light and dark themes at 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
+- Verify keyboard traversal, visible focus, menu invocation, Escape behavior, screen-reader labels, truncation, long localized text, and narrow-window behavior.
+- Status is never conveyed by color alone.
+
+### Regression coverage
+
+- Run `brand_tokens_tests`, `shell_theme_tests`, and the existing AgentUI tests required by the design-system guide.
+- Add focused native tests for the pane read model and commands.
+- Exercise the local multi-plate workflow end to end, including project metadata, physical-print history, version history, and export.
+- Use the fake-printer workflow in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` when printer-connected behavior is involved. Use an isolated `--datadir` and never drive another JusPrin instance.
+- If an OrcaSlicer-owned file changes, include the rebase evidence required by `fork-stewardship.md`.
+
+This is a temporary implementation handoff. Keep it untracked until Kenneth decides it is ready to commit.
*** End Patch";

# JusPrin left pane implementation handoff

Implement a native left pane in JusPrin's Prepare workspace, including an intentional collapsed state. The approved direction is a **Plates / Project** tabbed pane that is visible even for one plate and one object; the user alone chooses when to collapse it. Use the [JusPrin v2 Figma file](https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2?node-id=36-2) for final geometry, visual states, and component styling. The approved 25c/25f wireframes are design rationale; the Figma mockups and the behavior below are the handoff.

Figma states: [Two plates](https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2?node-id=36-2) (the original `maker-at-work-tools-attach` frame), [Project](https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2?node-id=1105-538), [count-only print history](https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2?node-id=1105-1973), [one plate expanded](https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2?node-id=1105-2457), and [left pane collapsed](https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2?node-id=1105-2787). The [future history frame](https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2?node-id=1105-2215) is illustrative only.

## Scope and behavior

| Area | First version |
| --- | --- |
| Plates tab | List every plate. The active plate is expanded to show its objects; inactive plates are compact. Show plate name/number and **Sliced** or **Needs slice**. Show object name and copy count. A plate row activates that plate; an object row selects it in the 3D view. Keep the highlight in sync when selection changes on the canvas. Offer a quiet **Add plate** action. |
| One-plate project | Show the same pane and tabs. Never remove it automatically because the project looks simple. |
| Special cases | If a copy is marked *won't print*, retain it in the project's count and expose that state when the object is expanded. Show a **Not on a plate** group only when an object exists there. Selecting an off-plate object should select it and bring it into view. These are project facts, not a general warning list. |
| Project tab | Show project name and save state, then **Printed N times**, **Details**, **Version history**, and **Export project 3MF…**. The first three open views inside the pane; each has a back control to the Project list. Export opens the existing system save dialog and leaves the pane on its current Project view. |
| Print history | Today's trustworthy baseline is the total count. In the count-only view, explain that details for older prints were not recorded. Figma's dated records, duration, filament, and cost are explicitly **future illustrative data**; do not render invented records or portray slice estimates as measured print facts. Add real rows only if authoritative persisted records for those exact fields are available. |
| Version history | Reuse the existing autosave history, restore, confirmation, and error behavior. If a version is previewed in the 3D view, distinguish it from the current project and offer **Restore** and **Back to current**. Do not silently replace the live project. |
| Collapse / expand | Provide a visible, accessible collapse control for the user. When collapsed, leave a small, unambiguous expand affordance at the left edge. The collapsed view must **not** say only “Object 1”; use the refined Figma state for its context. Collapse hides the pane contents without changing Orca selection, active plate, current tab/subview, or the 3D scene. Reopen restores the prior pane width and view. Do not auto-collapse or auto-expand on plate count, project changes, or navigation. Hide the pane on Home; returning to Prepare restores the user's collapsed/expanded choice. |

Keep printer, nozzle, filament, Slice/Print, import, object tools, and Agent conversation in their existing homes. Do not add a persistent button row for rename, duplicate, delete, arrange, or part/assembly management. The selected-object tool strip and Orca context menu already cover infrequent object actions; File > Import and drag/drop already add models. Preserve the selected 3D object when switching between Plates and Project.

## Navigation details

- Switching to **Project** changes only the left pane. The current plate and canvas selection remain intact. Switching back to **Plates** returns to that plate/object highlight.
- In a Project subview, **Back** or Escape goes up one level to the Project list. Escape at the Project list does not jump to Plates. The Plates tab always returns directly to the plate list.
- The Project tab may remember its last subview for the current app session; a new project should start at the Project list to avoid showing stale project facts.
- The pane's state is presentation state. Orca's project model, plate list, selection, slicing results, and undo history remain authoritative. Do not serialize a second project model or create a separate undo path.

## Code map and integration gaps

1. Add the pane as a fork-owned wxWidgets sibling of the existing workspace in [`ShellController.cpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp) / [`ShellController.hpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.hpp). The shell currently places the Notebook workspace, Agent resize handle, and Agent pane in `m_center_sizer`. Keep the stock Notebook pages and their selection intact. Mirror the existing Agent-pane hide/restore lifecycle where useful, with independent left-pane width/state.
2. Read authoritative state through [`Workspace.hpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/Workspace.hpp) and [`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp); use [`ProjectState.hpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectState.hpp) notifications to refresh after selection, plate, object, slice, undo/redo, and project replacement. Clear IDs tied to an old `project_session`.
3. The current workspace snapshot projects objects **only when an instance is inside a plate**. It has no off-plate group, per-copy printable flag/ID, or public plate-selection command; `select_object` selects the whole object. Extend the fork-owned projection/commands narrowly for the approved rows. Use Orca's plate membership, instance `printable` state, and selection mechanisms; do not infer them from names or canvas coordinates. A row that denotes one excluded copy must select that copy, not all copies.
4. The header's [`StatusRow.cpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp) currently owns Version history, Project details, Export project 3MF, and a passive print count in its kebab menu. Move those entry points to the Project tab while preserving the existing autosave/export/restore functionality and errors. **Export project 3MF** is separate from **Export sliced file** by the print action. Recent projects and Preferences can remain in the header menu.
5. The print ledger and count are exposed through [`ProjectStateDocument.hpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectStateDocument.hpp) and manufacturing history. Check which saved records are genuinely available. Build statistics may be estimates; label them accordingly rather than calling them actual print duration or cost. If subscribing to ledger changes, do not overwrite a listener another shell component needs.
6. The current shell hides Orca's legacy sidebar and canvas plate controls through [`CanvasPresentationController.cpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/CanvasPresentationController.cpp). The new pane must provide visible plate navigation without re-enabling those overlays. Preserve the existing [`ViewportToolStrip.cpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Canvas/ViewportToolStrip.cpp) actions and right-click path.

Follow [`README.md`](README.md), [`architecture.md`](architecture.md), and [`engineering-method.md`](engineering-method.md). Before changing an upstream-owned file, read [`fork-stewardship.md`](fork-stewardship.md) and keep the seam small and additive. Before UI code, follow [`design-system.md`](design-system.md): all colors, radii, fonts, and control sizes come from [`design-tokens.json`](../../resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json) through `ShellTheme`/shell recipes. Add a token and guard for any missing value instead of embedding a literal.

## Done when

- Compare the running UI with Figma at normal and collapsed widths, including one plate/one object, two plates, Project, count-only history, and a narrowed window. Verify readable focus, labels, and contrast in light and dark themes and high-DPI scaling.
- Exercise plate switching, object/copy selection from both pane and canvas, adding a plate, an excluded copy, an off-plate object, tab switching, collapse/reopen, Home/Prepare navigation, project replacement, undo/redo, and re-slicing. State must remain synchronized without stale highlights or IDs.
- Verify the existing Version history restore flow, 3MF export, project details, print count, and header menu changes end to end. Historical print rows must not appear unless backed by real stored facts.
- Run focused tests plus a local multi-plate shell workflow. Record any Figma/design gap that blocks a faithful implementation. If upstream-owned files change, include the rebase evidence required by `fork-stewardship.md`.

This is a working handoff document. Keep it untracked until Kenneth decides it is ready to commit.

- If a plate contains several distinct objects, show the object count used by Figma.
- Include disabled copies in the total. Append the separate **N won't print** phrase when applicable.
- Show lock or customized-plate-settings indicators only when those facts apply.
- **Add plate** must call Orca's existing plate creation path and participate in Orca undo/redo.

### Object rows and hierarchy

- Show the object name and copy count.
- Show filament/color assignment only for a multi-material job or an object-specific override.
- Make a disabled object's or copy's **won't print** state explicit.
- Show **Not on a plate** only when at least one object instance belongs to no plate. Membership comes from `PartPlateList`, not bounding-box guesses made by the pane.
- A simple object remains one row.
- Add disclosure children only for data that exists: copies, model parts, modifiers, negative parts, support enforcers, or support blockers.
- Do not introduce a permanent synthetic assembly level.
- Keep intentional customization separate from mesh problems. Implement the recommended `h2` treatment in frame 26h: one gray customization mark opens the list of applicable Orca tools/settings. Mesh problems use the distinct error treatment in Figma.

### Context menus

Use the menu contents and ordering from frames 26d1 and 26d2. Route every command to Orca's existing behavior rather than reimplementing it in the pane.

Plate menu:

- Rename
- Arrange
- Auto-orient
- Lock or Unlock
- Plate settings
- Delete plate
- Show Move to front and filament grouping only when their existing Orca preconditions apply.

Object menu:

- Use Orca's existing object context actions for quantity, printability, filament, per-object settings, repair, split, rename, and delete.
- A copy row exposes the same relevant menu path for that copy.
- Right-clicking a row and clicking its overflow button must open the same menu model.

## Project tab behavior

### Identity and metadata

- The saved JusPrin project name and save state come from managed project persistence. They are not the model title stored in the 3MF.
- The model title, designer/author, license, description, profile metadata, cover images, and packed files come from Orca's project metadata and `Workspace::ProjectDetails`.
- Never synthesize a model title from the project name or source filename.
- Omit missing metadata. Do not render blank fields or placeholders.
- When no model metadata exists, use frame 26f exactly and keep **Edit Project Info** available.
- **Details** opens the nested pane view in frame 26e2. Show only sections backed by data.
- Attachment categories should map to Orca's existing packed-file categories. Bill of materials, assembly guide, images, and other files remain Orca project attachments; do not copy them into a second store.
- **Edit Project Info** opens Orca's existing project-information editor.

### Project root actions

- **Printed N times** opens print history.
- **Details** opens project details.
- **Version history** opens the existing managed autosave history and preserves its current restore confirmation, pinning, validation, and failure behavior.
- **Export project 3MF…** opens the existing system save dialog and uses `ProjectAutosave::export_copy`. It is separate from exporting G-code or a sliced 3MF.
- Moving these entry points from `StatusRow` must preserve current functionality and error handling. Recent projects and Preferences may remain in the header overflow menu.

### Nested navigation

- A Project subview uses the back action shown in Figma to return to the Project root.
- Escape goes up one Project level when a subview is open.
- Escape at the Project root does not switch to Plates.
- Clicking the Plates tab always returns directly to the plate list while preserving plate and object selection.
- A new project starts on the Project root. Do not show a subview retained from the previous project.

## Print history truthfulness

`Agent::ProjectStateDocument::physical_prints()` is the authoritative physical-print ledger. Do not construct history from slice events, exports, or UI activity.

- The root count comes from `physical_print_count()`.
- A detailed row may show only fields present in its `PhysicalPrintRecord`: timestamps, plate, printer, outcome, and related recorded facts.
- Duration may be derived only when both recorded timestamps are valid.
- Material weight, cost, and predicted time in `SliceStatistics` are slice/build estimates. Label them as estimates as shown in frame 26e3; never present them as measured physical consumption or duration.
- Do not add a currency symbol unless the persisted record identifies the currency. A bare stored cost is not enough to guess dollars.
- Omit any missing field instead of substituting zero or placeholder copy.
- Preserve count-only history for migrated/older data. Use frame 26e4 when no detailed records exist, and the count-only row from 26e3 when detailed and legacy records coexist.
- Map outcomes to localized user-facing labels without losing the persisted distinction among `completed`, `failed`, and `cancelled`.
- Subscribe to ledger changes without taking away the listener needed by another shell component. If the existing single-listener persistence API cannot support both `StatusRow` and the pane during migration, replace it with safe multi-subscriber ownership before moving the count.

## Current code map and known gaps

Start with the canonical documents in `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`. Before changing an OrcaSlicer-owned file, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`.

Likely integration points:

- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp` and `.hpp`: place the fork-owned pane as the left sibling of the existing workspace. Keep the stock Notebook pages and Agent-pane lifecycle intact.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/Workspace.hpp`: extend the fork-owned projection with the smallest behavior-oriented data and commands the pane needs.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp`: read current plate membership, slice state, selection, object hierarchy, metadata, and customization facts; delegate mutations to their Orca owners.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectState.hpp`: refresh on Selection, Objects, Plates, Project, Settings, History, Transform, undo/redo, slicing, and project replacement as relevant.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp`: migrate Project entry points and print count after the pane owns them, without changing Recent projects, Preferences, or unrelated header behavior.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ManufacturingHistory.hpp` and `ProjectStateDocument.hpp`: read physical-print records and counts.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/CanvasPresentationController.cpp`: keep the legacy Orca sidebar and plate overlays hidden; the new pane supplies visible navigation.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Canvas/ViewportToolStrip.cpp`: preserve the existing object tools and right-click path.

The current workspace snapshot is not sufficient for every approved row. Confirm and close these gaps before building presentation code around assumptions:

1. `WorkspacePlate::objects` does not expose per-instance IDs, per-instance printability, or off-plate instances.
2. `ObjectDetails` exposes counts but not the named child rows needed for parts, modifiers, negative parts, or support volumes.
3. Plate selection and all row-menu commands do not yet share one public UI command surface.
4. Intentional customization needs explicit facts for support painting, color painting, variable layer height, per-object overrides, and plate settings.
5. Mesh repair/problem status needs a stable read model separate from customization state.
6. Project metadata exposes attachment identifiers and categories; the pane still needs the existing Orca paths that open each detail or attachment.

Expose the smallest strict API that represents each missing fact or command. Keep preconditions in the caller that owns the workflow and let unexpected failures remain visible.

## Design-system and component rules

Follow `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` before writing UI code.

- Every color, radius, font, and control size comes from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json` through `ShellTheme` or `ShellRecipes`.
- Layout gaps use the documented spacing scale.
- If a required value has no token, add the token and its guard before using it.
- Reuse established generic primitives such as icons, icon buttons, tabs, menus, swatches, typography, and selection treatments.
- Keep feature-specific plate rows, object rows, metadata blocks, and history records as pane-owned composition unless another production surface already has the same reusable contract.
- Do not add Figma-style specimen components or one-off variants to the production design system merely because several mockup frames repeat a structure.
- Support light and dark themes, keyboard focus, localization, and 100%, 150%, and 200% display scaling.

## Suggested implementation order

1. Add tests for the missing read model: plate membership, per-copy printability, folded summaries, off-plate instances, hierarchy counts/children, customization facts, and mesh-problem status.
2. Add the smallest workspace commands for plate selection/addition and menu actions that do not already have a fork-owned seam.
3. Build the pane shell and tab/navigation state using frame 26c1 first.
4. Add the ordinary and folded multi-plate states from 26a and 26c2.
5. Add complex object hierarchy and conditional indicators from 26b and 26h.
6. Route the menus from 26d1 and 26d2 to existing Orca actions.
7. Add the Project root and metadata states from 26e1, 26e2, and 26f.
8. Move version history/export/details/count entry points from `StatusRow` only after their pane replacements pass end-to-end tests.
9. Add print history from the persisted ledger using 26e3 and 26e4.
10. Run visual and behavioral verification across supported platforms and scaling levels.

## Acceptance criteria

### Behavior

- One plate and one object still show the pane and both tabs.
- Plate selection, object selection, canvas selection, active plate, and row highlights stay synchronized in both directions.
- Folded summaries remain correct after add, delete, duplicate, disable, move between plates, arrange, undo/redo, project restore, and project replacement.
- Simple objects stay simple. Child rows appear only for existing copies, parts, modifiers, negative parts, and support volumes.
- Not on a plate appears only with real off-plate content.
- Every plate and object menu action reaches the existing Orca behavior and undo history.
- Project name and 3MF model title never substitute for one another.
- Missing metadata uses 26f without invented or blank values.
- Version restore and project export preserve existing confirmations, validation, and failure behavior.
- Print history displays only persisted facts and clearly labeled estimates.
- Frame 26g behavior is absent.

### Visual and accessibility

- Compare every implemented state against its named Figma frame.
- Verify light and dark themes at 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- Verify keyboard traversal, visible focus, menu invocation, Escape behavior, screen-reader labels, truncation, long localized text, and narrow-window behavior.
- Status is never conveyed by color alone.

### Regression coverage

- Run `brand_tokens_tests`, `shell_theme_tests`, and the existing AgentUI tests required by the design-system guide.
- Add focused native tests for the pane read model and commands.
- Exercise the local multi-plate workflow end to end, including project metadata, physical-print history, version history, and export.
- Use the fake-printer workflow in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` when printer-connected behavior is involved. Use an isolated `--datadir` and never drive another JusPrin instance.
- If an OrcaSlicer-owned file changes, include the rebase evidence required by `fork-stewardship.md`.

This is a temporary implementation handoff. Keep it untracked until Kenneth decides it is ready to commit.

## My request:
Now review your process of working with figma agent. Summarize what you did well and what you could have done better.

## What went well

- **I followed the one-step-at-a-time workflow.** Each prompt covered one coherent state or comparison, and I visually inspected the result before continuing.
- **I used the wireframe as the behavioral source.** The prompts preserved exact names, menu ordering, conditional content, metadata rules, and print-history distinctions.
- **I corrected visible mistakes instead of trusting the agent’s summary.** Examples included menu placement, truncated labels, disclosure direction, selection styling, and missing copy counts.
- **I preserved the approved workspace shell.** New frames consistently reused the existing viewport, header, right panel, tokens, and proportions.
- **I kept 26g out of the work.** No collapse rail or collapse control entered the final mockups or implementation handoff.
- **I responded to the component concern.** I removed the feature-specific components and specimens created earlier, then required subsequent pane content to remain ordinary editable groups using existing generic primitives.
- **I handled nonvisual requirements explicitly.** The Project frames distinguish the saved project name from 3MF metadata, and print history distinguishes recorded facts from slice estimates.
- **I ended with a complete, verified set of frames.** The ordinary, complex, folded, menu, metadata, history, empty, and customization states all received individual visual checks.

## What could have been better

- **I over-componentized the early work.** I treated repeated mockup structures as reusable design-system components before proving they had a broader product use. That added noise and required cleanup.
- **I interpreted “one step at a time” too literally at first.** I could have grouped closely related states, such as the two 26c variants or Project history variants, while still pausing for verification at meaningful design decisions.
- **The prompts were often longer than necessary.** Repeating the same shell-preservation and no-component constraints reduced the agent’s attention available for the state-specific requirements. A persistent short rules block plus a focused delta would have been clearer.
- **I let the Figma agent repeatedly search the design system.** After the first audit, I should have referenced a stable list of approved primitives and told it to reuse those directly.
- **I did not establish reuse criteria before starting.** A better initial rule would have been: only create a design-system component when it already has at least two independent product consumers and a stable behavioral contract.
- **I could have planned the frame set before execution.** A short frame inventory and dependency order would have reduced navigation overhead and made progress easier to review.
- **I did not record frame links as they were created.** I later had frame names but not a complete node-link index. Capturing each node URL immediately would have improved the implementation handoff.
- **I could have checked implementation truth earlier.** The detailed print-history mockup includes plausible sample data, while the implementation must display only persisted facts. I resolved this in the handoff, but raising it during the Figma work would have made the design intent clearer.
- **Some visual checks were inefficient.** I repeatedly hid the Figma interface, zoomed to the frame, then drilled into the pane. A consistent review viewport or dedicated review section would have reduced tool operations.
- **I should have paused sooner after the user’s concern.** The component cleanup was correct, but I could have immediately summarized the new component policy before continuing so the user could validate the direction.

## Better process next time

1. Audit the wireframe and existing design system once.
2. Define a strict reuse rule before creating anything.
3. Make a frame checklist with exact Figma names and capture each node URL.
4. Give the agent a short persistent rules block.
5. Prompt only for the current state’s differences.
6. Verify each meaningful interaction pattern, while grouping simple variants.
7. Record corrections and implementation caveats as the work progresses.
8. Run a final consistency review across all frames before producing the handoff.

## What went well

- **I followed the one-step-at-a-time workflow.** Each prompt covered one coherent state or comparison, and I visually inspected the result before continuing.
- **I used the wireframe as the behavioral source.** The prompts preserved exact names, menu ordering, conditional content, metadata rules, and print-history distinctions.
- **I corrected visible mistakes instead of trusting the agent’s summary.** Examples included menu placement, truncated labels, disclosure direction, selection styling, and missing copy counts.
- **I preserved the approved workspace shell.** New frames consistently reused the existing viewport, header, right panel, tokens, and proportions.
- **I kept 26g out of the work.** No collapse rail or collapse control entered the final mockups or implementation handoff.
- **I responded to the component concern.** I removed the feature-specific components and specimens created earlier, then required subsequent pane content to remain ordinary editable groups using existing generic primitives.
- **I handled nonvisual requirements explicitly.** The Project frames distinguish the saved project name from 3MF metadata, and print history distinguishes recorded facts from slice estimates.
- **I ended with a complete, verified set of frames.** The ordinary, complex, folded, menu, metadata, history, empty, and customization states all received individual visual checks.

## What could have been better

- **I over-componentized the early work.** I treated repeated mockup structures as reusable design-system components before proving they had a broader product use. That added noise and required cleanup.
- **I interpreted “one step at a time” too literally at first.** I could have grouped closely related states, such as the two 26c variants or Project history variants, while still pausing for verification at meaningful design decisions.
- **The prompts were often longer than necessary.** Repeating the same shell-preservation and no-component constraints reduced the agent’s attention available for the state-specific requirements. A persistent short rules block plus a focused delta would have been clearer.
- **I let the Figma agent repeatedly search the design system.** After the first audit, I should have referenced a stable list of approved primitives and told it to reuse those directly.
- **I did not establish reuse criteria before starting.** A better initial rule would have been: only create a design-system component when it already has at least two independent product consumers and a stable behavioral contract.
- **I could have planned the frame set before execution.** A short frame inventory and dependency order would have reduced navigation overhead and made progress easier to review.
- **I did not record frame links as they were created.** I later had frame names but not a complete node-link index. Capturing each node URL immediately would have improved the implementation handoff.
- **I could have checked implementation truth earlier.** The detailed print-history mockup includes plausible sample data, while the implementation must display only persisted facts. I resolved this in the handoff, but raising it during the Figma work would have made the design intent clearer.
- **Some visual checks were inefficient.** I repeatedly hid the Figma interface, zoomed to the frame, then drilled into the pane. A consistent review viewport or dedicated review section would have reduced tool operations.
- **I should have paused sooner after the user’s concern.** The component cleanup was correct, but I could have immediately summarized the new component policy before continuing so the user could validate the direction.

## Better process next time

1. Audit the wireframe and existing design system once.
2. Define a strict reuse rule before creating anything.
3. Make a frame checklist with exact Figma names and capture each node URL.
4. Give the agent a short persistent rules block.
5. Prompt only for the current state’s differences.
6. Verify each meaningful interaction pattern, while grouping simple variants.
7. Record corrections and implementation caveats as the work progresses.
8. Run a final consistency review across all frames before producing the handoff.

---
name: skill-creator
description: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources.
metadata:
  short-description: Create or update a skill
---

# Skill Creator

Create skills that give Codex useful, non-obvious guidance without constraining unrelated work.

## Core Principles

**Assume Codex is already capable.** Include only information that changes its decisions or improves its work. Remove generic advice, repeated instructions, speculative edge cases, and examples that do not materially clarify the task.

**Preserve user intent and scope.** A skill should support the requested task, not replace the user's chosen product, expand the assignment, modify unrelated configuration, or imply permission for additional external actions. Do not turn a particular example, past failure, or personal preference into a universal requirement.

Approval to complete a task does not expand its scope or execution permissions. For retrying or externally mutating workflows, define a stopping condition proportional to the risk.

**Match specificity to the risk.** Give the model room to choose an appropriate approach when multiple approaches are reasonable. Use detailed steps, deterministic scripts, or absolute language only when correctness, safety, permissions, or a genuinely fragile workflow requires them.

For open-ended work, describe the outcome and relevant decision criteria. For workflows with a preferred shape, offer useful examples or configurable scripts. Reserve fixed sequences and narrow parameters for operations where deviation would cause a concrete problem. Preserve non-obvious operational invariants, distinguish actual requirements from optional recommendations or local conventions, and avoid restating policies already enforced elsewhere.

**Keep discovery cheap and precise.** Skill names and descriptions are available before a skill is loaded. Describe the actual capability and when it applies, adding exclusions only when they prevent likely misrouting. Avoid exhaustive capability lists and catchalls that attract unrelated requests.

Keep skills self-contained; refer to another skill or tool only when the requested workflow genuinely requires it and it is available in the target environment. Specialized review, hardening, or audit workflows should apply when requested or genuinely needed, not merely because ordinary work touches the same subject.

**Disclose detail progressively.** Keep shared purpose, essential constraints, and useful routing in `SKILL.md`. Put substantial mode-specific guidance, schemas, examples, or procedures in supporting references and read only the references relevant to the current task. A simple self-contained skill does not need a router or extra files.

## Anatomy of a Skill

Every skill is a folder containing a required `SKILL.md` file and any optional resources its actual workflow needs:

```text
skill-name/
|-- SKILL.md                 Required skill instructions
|   |-- YAML frontmatter     Required name and description
|   `-- Markdown body        Instructions loaded when the skill is used
|-- agents/                  Optional UI metadata and invocation policy
|   `-- openai.yaml
|-- scripts/                 Optional executable helpers
|-- references/              Optional documentation loaded as needed
`-- assets/                  Optional files used in generated output
```

Choose the structure that fits the actual task. Some skills are short and self-contained; others route among operating modes or delegate complex mechanics to scripts. Avoid creating directories, placeholders, examples, or ancillary documentation without a clear use.

### SKILL.md

The YAML frontmatter identifies the skill and determines when it should be considered. Include the required `name` and `description`, and preserve supported optional fields such as existing `metadata` when appropriate.

The Markdown body is loaded only when the skill is used. Put the purpose, essential workflow, real constraints, and useful links there. Keep detailed procedures and examples in supporting references when they are relevant only to particular modes.

Skill information is disclosed in three stages:

1. **Name and description:** Available during skill selection, so keep them concise and discriminating.
2. **SKILL.md body:** Loaded when the skill applies, so keep its instructions relevant to that task.
3. **Supporting resources:** Read or execute only when the current task actually needs them.

The entrypoint should be as short as the task permits while retaining important constraints. A large upper bound is not a target: move conditional detail into references when doing so improves clarity or context use, rather than waiting for the file to become unwieldy.

### Scripts

Use `scripts/` for executable code when the same logic would otherwise be rewritten repeatedly or deterministic execution materially improves reliability.

- **Example:** `scripts/rotate_pdf.py` for a PDF operation that would otherwise require recreating the same code.
- **Useful for:** Repeated transformations, reliable API operations, data processing, and other concrete automation.
- **Validation:** Run new or changed scripts to verify their behavior. Scripts can usually be executed without loading their full implementation into context, although an agent may need to inspect them when patching or adapting them.

### References

Use `references/` for documentation that is needed only in particular contexts.

- **Examples:** `references/schema.md` for database tables, `references/policies.md` for domain rules, `references/api_docs.md` for an API, or separate writing guides for different deliverables.
- **Useful for:** Schemas, API documentation, company policies, format-specific procedures, detailed workflows, and substantial examples.
- **Routing:** Link each reference from `SKILL.md` or another relevant resource and explain when it should be read. Keep information in one place instead of duplicating it across the entrypoint and references.

Keep references focused on maintained, task-specific information that changes the agent's decisions. Avoid copied manuals, exhaustive catalogs, and generic tutorials already available from authoritative sources. Before removing existing resources, inspect their callers and purpose.

For large references, include useful search terms or a short contents section when that makes the needed material easier to find.

### Assets

Use `assets/` for files that belong in generated output rather than in the model's instructions.

- **Examples:** `assets/logo.png`, `assets/slides.pptx`, `assets/font.ttf`, or `assets/frontend-template/`.
- **Useful for:** Templates, images, fonts, icons, boilerplate projects, and other files copied or adapted into the result.
- **Context:** Do not load assets as instructions unless the task requires inspecting them.

### UI Metadata and Invocation Policy

`agents/openai.yaml` can provide UI-facing metadata such as `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt`, along with invocation policy. When creating or updating those settings, read [references/openai_yaml.md](references/openai_yaml.md) and keep the values consistent with the skill.

Automatic skill selection is allowed by default. Change that default only when the user explicitly requests an explicit-only skill:

```yaml
policy:
  allow_implicit_invocation: false
```

This keeps the skill available when explicitly invoked as `$skill-name` without adding it to the model context automatically. Preserve unrelated existing UI, policy, and dependency fields when updating `agents/openai.yaml`.

The initializer creates this file automatically. For new or interface-only metadata, generate it with:

```bash
scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py <path/to/skill-folder> --interface key=value
```

The generator replaces the entire file. If an existing file contains `policy` or `dependencies`, update only the intended fields in place instead of regenerating it.

Include optional interface fields only when the user provides or requests them.

### What Not to Include

Include files that directly support the skill's work. Avoid adding a `README.md`, installation guide, changelog, duplicated quick reference, or other auxiliary documentation unless a specific task or packaging requirement calls for it.

## Progressive Disclosure in Practice

For a skill with multiple substantial modes, keep the shared guidance and mode-selection criteria in `SKILL.md`. Link each supporting reference where its use becomes relevant. Do not load every reference by default, duplicate reference content in the entrypoint, or add a routing layer when there is nothing meaningful to route.

For example, a deployment skill can keep provider selection in `SKILL.md` and separate provider details:

```text
cloud-deploy/
|-- SKILL.md
`-- references/
    |-- aws.md
    |-- gcp.md
    `-- azure.md
```

When the user chooses AWS, read `references/aws.md`; do not also load the GCP and Azure guides. The same pattern can separate business domains, deliverable types, or other genuinely distinct operating modes.

A short skill can instead route to details only when an advanced operation needs them:

```markdown
## Documents

Handle ordinary edits directly.

- For tracked changes, read [references/redlining.md](references/redlining.md).
- For document internals, read [references/ooxml.md](references/ooxml.md).
```

These examples illustrate options, not a required structure. Choose the organization that makes the skill easier to use without loading irrelevant material.

## Create or Update a Skill

Adapt the work to the request. Creating a complex new skill may involve understanding realistic use cases, choosing supporting resources, initializing files, writing instructions, and validating the result. A narrow update to an existing skill may require only a focused edit and validation.

Ask clarifying questions only when the missing information matters and cannot be reasonably inferred. Respect a user-specified location; otherwise create discoverable skills in `$CODEX_HOME/skills`, or `~/.codex/skills` when `CODEX_HOME` is unset.

Keep automatic skill selection enabled unless the user explicitly requests an explicit-only skill. When the intended invocation mode is genuinely unclear and matters to the requested workflow, ask whether the user wants normal automatic discovery or explicit-only invocation; otherwise preserve the default. Do not infer explicit-only invocation from sensitive operations or required approvals: keep the skill discoverable and require authorization immediately before the actual mutation. Preserve an existing skill's invocation policy unless the user asks to change it.

For a new or substantially revised skill, consider the actual requests it should handle and which reusable resources would improve those tasks:

- A repeated PDF transformation may justify a `scripts/rotate_pdf.py` helper.
- An application-building workflow may benefit from an `assets/frontend-template/` starter.
- A data-analysis skill may need a `references/schema.md` guide to avoid rediscovering table relationships.

Create those resources only when their concrete benefit justifies them. If the user has already explained the task clearly, proceed without requesting additional examples.

### Naming

- Use lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.
- Keep names under 64 characters and prefer short action-oriented names.
- Namespace by tool or domain when doing so improves discovery.
- Name the skill folder after the skill.

### Initialize a New Skill

For a new skill, use the bundled initializer when it helps create the required files consistently:

```bash
scripts/init_skill.py <skill-name> --path <output-directory> [--resources scripts,references,assets] [--examples]
```

For example:

```bash
scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills"
scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills" --resources references
```

Request only the resource directories the skill needs. Use `--examples` only when concrete placeholders would help, and replace or remove them before finishing. Do not initialize an existing skill again.

The initializer creates the skill directory, a concise `SKILL.md` starter, and `agents/openai.yaml`. It creates resource directories and example files only when requested. Pass generated UI values as `--interface key=value` when needed.

### Write the Instructions

The frontmatter `description` should briefly explain what the skill does and when it applies. Include a meaningful boundary when similar requests should not activate the skill.

For example:

```yaml
description: Create or edit Word documents when formatting, tracked changes, or comments require document-specific handling.
```

Put detailed workflows, tool choices, examples, and operating modes in the body or relevant references rather than listing them all in the description. Preserve supported optional frontmatter, such as existing `metadata`, when appropriate.

Write only the instructions needed for another Codex instance to perform the task well. State the desired outcome, non-obvious context, real constraints, and relevant references or tools. Preserve the user's explicit choices and existing authorization boundaries. Avoid prescribing a fixed structure, process, or number of steps when the task does not require one.

### Validate and Iterate

Validate the completed skill with:

```bash
scripts/quick_validate.py <path/to/skill-folder>
```

The validator checks frontmatter, naming, and unfinished scaffold placeholders; it does not prove that the skill makes good decisions. Also check that descriptions remain discriminating, instructions preserve user intent, references are discoverable, and any added scripts actually work.

When testing is warranted, verify observable behavior or meaningful invariants. Avoid tests that merely match generated wording, headings, or regex patterns.

Improve the skill based on real usage or demonstrated failures. Prefer a narrow correction to accumulating universal rules for every observed example.

## Independent Forward-Testing

Use an independent subagent pass when a skill is sufficiently complex or risky that realistic behavioral validation would add meaningful confidence, and when delegation is available and authorized. Ordinary creation or small edits do not automatically require subagents.

Give the evaluating agent a realistic user request, the skill, and the minimum raw artifacts needed to perform the task. Do not provide the intended answer, suspected bug, proposed fix, or prior conclusions unless the evaluation genuinely requires them.

For example:

```text
Use $skill-name at /path/to/skill-name to complete this realistic request.
```

Keep the evaluation scoped to permitted resources and side effects. Use an isolated temporary workspace for generated artifacts so they do not enter the working tree or contaminate later evaluations. Ask for approval when the proposed evaluation would require additional authorization, affect a live production system, or impose substantial time or cost. Review the actual outcome and artifacts, then make only changes supported by the observed behavior.

+
+Use this guide to decide whether Figma Agent should reuse, compose, extend, or leave a design local.

+## Classify the thing before building it
+
+### Token or style
+
+A semantic value used across unrelated surfaces: color intent, typography role, spacing scale, radius, elevation, or control sizing.

+Reuse the existing semantic value. Add a new one only when the product needs a new semantic role, not because one mockup needs a slightly different number.
+
+### Generic primitive
+
+A small control with a stable interaction contract across features: icon button, tab, menu row, popover, checkbox, badge, disclosure, text role, or swatch.
+
+Reuse the existing primitive. If none exists, promotion can be justified when independent product surfaces need the same behavior and state model.
+
+### Feature composition
+
+A combination whose meaning belongs to one feature: a plate row, project metadata preview, print-history record, account summary, or domain-specific card.
+
+Keep it in the feature as ordinary auto-layout frames/groups or a feature-local component when implementation-oriented prototyping truly benefits from local reuse. Do not put it in the shared design system merely because it repeats across several states of the same feature.
+
+### One-off state
+
+A menu-open example, empty state, comparison alternative, annotation, or review specimen.
+
+Keep it local and ordinary. It does not belong in the shared library.
+
+## Promotion test
+
+Promote a new item to the shared design system only when all relevant answers are yes:
+
+1. **Independent reuse:** at least two separate product contexts need it, or the user explicitly requests a shared primitive.
+2. **Stable contract:** its purpose, anatomy, interaction, and state model are understood.
+3. **Meaningful variants:** variants represent real reusable states, not different example content.
+4. **Token fit:** it uses established semantic variables, or a justified new semantic role is being added.
+5. **Ownership:** there is a clear library location and name that future designers can discover.
+6. **Maintenance value:** promotion reduces future divergence more than it increases library search noise.
+
+If the evidence is incomplete, keep the design local. Promotion can happen later without losing the work.
+

+- Components named after a numbered mockup or a single feature state.
+- A component created because an element appears twice in one flow.
+- Variants whose only difference is example text, object name, or count.
+- Specimen frames created during delivery even though no library documentation was requested.
+- Near-duplicate primitives differing by one spacing or color value.
+- Feature rows mixed into the same section as generic buttons, inputs, and menus.
+- Detached copies of an established primitive used to bypass its contract.
+- New raw color, typography, radius, or spacing styles that duplicate semantic variables.

+
+1. Search the local file and enabled libraries for the required primitive.

+
+Use ordinary editable groups and existing primitives. Select the corrected frame or frames and stop.

# Design-system governance for Figma Agent work

Use this guide to decide whether Figma Agent should reuse, compose, extend, or leave a design local.

## Classify the thing before building it

### Token or style

A semantic value used across unrelated surfaces: color intent, typography role, spacing scale, radius, elevation, or control sizing.

Reuse the existing semantic value. Add a new one only when the product needs a new semantic role, not because one mockup needs a slightly different number.

### Generic primitive

A small control with a stable interaction contract across features: icon button, tab, menu row, popover, checkbox, badge, disclosure, text role, or swatch.

Reuse the existing primitive. If none exists, promotion can be justified when independent product surfaces need the same behavior and state model.

### Feature composition

A combination whose meaning belongs to one feature: a plate row, project metadata preview, print-history record, account summary, or domain-specific card.

Keep it in the feature as ordinary auto-layout frames/groups or a feature-local component when implementation-oriented prototyping truly benefits from local reuse. Do not put it in the shared design system merely because it repeats across several states of the same feature.

### One-off state

A menu-open example, empty state, comparison alternative, annotation, or review specimen.

Keep it local and ordinary. It does not belong in the shared library.

## Promotion test

Promote a new item to the shared design system only when all relevant answers are yes:

1. **Independent reuse:** at least two separate product contexts need it, or the user explicitly requests a shared primitive.
2. **Stable contract:** its purpose, anatomy, interaction, and state model are understood.
3. **Meaningful variants:** variants represent real reusable states, not different example content.
4. **Token fit:** it uses established semantic variables, or a justified new semantic role is being added.
5. **Ownership:** there is a clear library location and name that future designers can discover.
6. **Maintenance value:** promotion reduces future divergence more than it increases library search noise.

If the evidence is incomplete, keep the design local. Promotion can happen later without losing the work.

## Signs of design-system pollution

- Components named after a numbered mockup or a single feature state.
- A component created because an element appears twice in one flow.
- Variants whose only difference is example text, object name, or count.
- Specimen frames created during delivery even though no library documentation was requested.
- Near-duplicate primitives differing by one spacing or color value.
- Feature rows mixed into the same section as generic buttons, inputs, and menus.
- Detached copies of an established primitive used to bypass its contract.
- New raw color, typography, radius, or spacing styles that duplicate semantic variables.

## Audit sequence

Before creation:

1. Search the local file and enabled libraries for the required primitive.
2. Inspect available properties and variants rather than judging from the component name alone.
3. Identify the nearest approved source frame using the same visual language.
4. Record any actual primitive gap separately from feature needs.

After each Figma Agent step:

1. Inspect the new frame's layers and instances.
2. Check the Assets or design-system page for unexpected definitions.
3. Confirm new feature structures are ordinary frames/groups unless promotion was deliberate.
4. Confirm established components were not modified globally.

At completion:

1. List every design-system addition.
2. State its independent consumers and contract.
3. Remove or demote any addition that fails the promotion test.

## Adding a genuinely missing primitive

When promotion is justified, give Figma Agent a separate bounded task:

- name the library section;
- define the primitive's purpose and anatomy;
- define only real states and properties;
- bind it to existing semantic variables;
- create a minimal specimen or documentation frame only if the library already uses one;
- replace local provisional versions with instances;
- verify existing components and frames remain unchanged.

Complete and verify this task before using the primitive broadly.
